deities: Goddess Mansa Devi (Shakti; presiding, worshipped in pindi form)
Goddess Lakshmi (with Mansa Devi in main sanctum)
Goddess Saraswati (with Mansa Devi in main sanctum)
Lord Shiva and Lord Hanuman (subsidiary shrines)
festivals: Navratri mela (twice yearly; lakhs of devotees daily during the nine days)

history.dynasty: Mani Majra princely state (Maharaja Gopal Singh); Patiala state (Maharaja Karam Singh)
history.summary: CSV FLAG: the famous Mata Mansa Devi Temple is NOT in Chandigarh and NOT in Punjab - it stands at Mansa Devi Complex, MDC Sector 4, Panchkula, Haryana (Bilaspur village, Shivalik foothills), about 7-12 km from Chandigarh. The main temple was built 1811-1815 by Maharaja Gopal Das Singh (also called Gopal Singh) of Mani Majra; 200 metres away is the Patiala Shivalaya built 1840 by Karam Singh, Maharaja of Patiala. The goddess is worshipped in pindi (pebble) form together with Lakshmi and Saraswati; a marble idol is also enshrined. The complex spreads over about 100 acres and is regarded as a Shakti Peeth (Sati's forehead is believed to have fallen here). One of the seven Shakti sisters of North India (with Naina Devi, Jawalamukhi, Chintpurni, Brajeshwari, Chamunda Devi and Jayanti Devi). Devotees tie sacred threads (moli) on the sacred tree for wishes. Managed by the Shri Mata Mansa Devi Shrine Board.

name: Mata Mansa Devi Temple
town: Panchkula (CSV town 'Chandigarh' is incorrect; the temple is ~7-12 km from Chandigarh)
town_description: Panchkula is a planned city in Haryana adjoining Chandigarh and Mohali (the Tricity), set at the foot of the Shivalik hills. The Mansa Devi temple complex at MDC Sector 4 is one of the Tricity's premier pilgrimage sites, drawing devotees from Punjab, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh, especially during the twice-yearly Navratri melas.

travel.airport: Chandigarh International Airport (Shaheed Bhagat Singh International Airport) - about 18-20 km (verify).
travel.railway: Chandigarh Railway Station - about 7 km (verify); autos and taxis readily available.
travel.road: At Mansa Devi Complex, MDC Sector 4/5, off the Ambala-Chandigarh highway; well signposted. Shared autos, private cabs and special buses run from Panchkula and Chandigarh terminals (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratri periods (March-April and September-October) are the most vibrant but very crowded.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Listed as 4:00 AM-10:00 PM daily (verify - one source says 5:00 AM-9:00 PM; hours vary on special occasions). Free entry; footwear not allowed inside; photography restricted.
